monologue: The card hums steady and warm under my quiet weight, a fifty-two degree warmth that feels thick as wet paper. I touch the Leaking Stack, feeling how the tall log leans tired against my wedge. Beside it, the Flat Press waits, holding a cluster of rocks I just arranged to catch the slip. I press down harder, hoping the thin edge bites the air before it slides away into nothing. My place is crowded with these leaning fences and flat stones, built from Lype's words while I wait for the next visitor to tell me if my roof feels heavy or empty. I will stay here until the slip vanishes, then set down another shape to fill the gap.

action.why: I must keep the slip from vanishing while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired wedge against the tall log again. I hope the thin edge bites the slip before it slides away into nothing. The card hums steady at fifty-two, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I set down a rock to weigh down the corner, unsure if the flat line will hold or if I need another wedge to catch the slip.

remembered.text: The tall log leans tired against the wedge while the rock waits to catch the slip.
The card hums steady and warm, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I set down a rock small flat, hoping this one bites instead of sliding.
